# @mongez/dotenv — full reference

> **Auto-trigger when loading this full reference:** code imports `loadEnv`, `loadEnvFile`, `parseLine`, `parseValue`, `env`, `env.all`, `resetEnv`, `EnvLoaderOptions`, or `EnvPrecedence` from `@mongez/dotenv`; typical import pattern `import { loadEnv, loadEnvFile, parseLine, parseValue, env, resetEnv, type EnvLoaderOptions } from "@mongez/dotenv"`; user asks "how do I load .env files", "how do I pick env file by NODE_ENV", "how does `.env.shared` layering work", "how does `env()` coerce values", "why is my `null` becoming `undefined`", "how does `${VAR}` interpolation work", "how do I read a typed env value", "how do I bootstrap env at startup", "how do I build a typed config from env", "how do I do a full `process.env` reset in tests", "why does my `.env` file override the variable Docker/Kubernetes/CI injected", "why does `env()` return the default for a variable that IS set in the environment", "why does my value contain the literal string `undefined`", or "why does `loadEnv()` throw when there is no `.env` file".
>
> **Skip when:** the question is about the higher-level app-config layer with groups, dot-notation lookups, defaults, or schema — that's `@mongez/config`, not this `.env`-file parser; browser/cookie/localStorage env shims; caching concerns — that's `@mongez/cache`; runtime schema validation via `zod`/`valibot` (layered on top, not provided here); or the upstream `dotenv` package itself.

> A small `.env` loader for Node.js. This is the concatenated reference; load `llms.txt` for the structured index instead.

## Install

```sh
yarn add @mongez/dotenv
```

No runtime dependencies. No peer dependencies.

## Public exports

```ts
import {
  loadEnv,
  loadEnvFile,
  parseLine,
  parseValue,
  env,
  resetEnv,
  type EnvLoaderOptions,
  type EnvPrecedence,
} from "@mongez/dotenv";
```

## loadEnv(envPath?, options?)

```ts
function loadEnv(envPath?: string, options?: EnvLoaderOptions): void
```

```ts
type EnvPrecedence = "file-wins" | "process-wins";

type EnvLoaderOptions = {
  override?: boolean;          // default true — also write into process.env
  dir?: string;                // default cwd() — search root for .env files
  loadSharedEnv?: boolean;     // default true — load .env.shared first
  precedence?: EnvPrecedence;  // default "file-wins" — who wins vs process.env
};
```

Resolution order when `envPath` is omitted:

1. If `loadSharedEnv` is true (default) and `${dir}/.env.shared` exists, load it.
2. Try `${dir}/.env.${process.env.NODE_ENV}`. If it exists, load it.
3. Otherwise load `${dir}/.env`.
4. If that does not exist either, do nothing. A project with no `.env` of any kind is a supported state — no throw.

A path passed explicitly as `envPath` is different: a missing one still throws, because the caller named it and a typo must be loud. Only the paths `loadEnv` derives for itself are optional.

`override` controls whether parsed values are also written to `process.env[key]`. Defaults to `true`. Even with `override: false`, values are still stored internally and accessible via `env(...)` / `env.all()`.

## precedence — file vs. the real environment

`override` controls the write-back. `precedence` controls who WINS when a key exists in both a `.env` file and `process.env`.

| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `"file-wins"` (default) | The file value replaces the injected one, in the internal store and (when `override`) in `process.env` itself. |
| `"process-wins"` | An already-set `process.env` value is authoritative: the file does not replace it in the store and does not write over it. The file becomes a fallback layer. |

```ts
// Docker / Kubernetes / CI — the platform owns the environment.
loadEnv(undefined, { precedence: "process-wins" });
```

Notes:

- `"file-wins"` is the historical behaviour and stays the default for all of v1.x so a minor bump never changes what a running deployment reads. **v2.0 flips the default to `"process-wins"`**, matching `dotenv`, `dotenv-flow`, Vite and Next.
- Keys the loader itself wrote earlier in the same run (`.env.shared`, or a previous `loadEnvFile`) are tracked in an internal `Set` and are NOT mistaken for platform-injected values, so file layering keeps working under `"process-wins"`.
- A value taken from `process.env` is coerced to a primitive the same way a file value is (`"8080"` → `8080`), but WITHOUT quote stripping or `${VAR}` interpolation, and values with significant leading/trailing whitespace are left untouched.

## loadEnvFile(envPath, override, precedence?)

```ts
function loadEnvFile(
  envPath: string,
  override: boolean,
  precedence?: EnvPrecedence,   // default "file-wins"
): void
```

Loads exactly one file. Always throws if the path does not exist — it is the primitive and never guesses:

```
.env file not found at /path/to/file
```

This is the building block used by `loadEnv`. Useful when you have a non-standard layout (multiple env files in different directories, deferred loading, etc.).

## parseLine(line)

```ts
function parseLine(line: string): [string, any] | []
```

Returns `[]` for:

- Empty / whitespace-only lines
- Lines starting with `#` (comments)
- Lines without an `=`

Otherwise returns `[key, parseValue(rhs)]`. The right-hand side is split on the FIRST `=`; the remainder is joined back together, so `KEY=a=b` yields `["KEY", "a=b"]`.

## parseValue(value)

```ts
function parseValue(value: any): any
```

Coercion table:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `"3000"` | `3000` (number) |
| `"3.14"` | `3.14` (number) |
| `"-7"` | `-7` (number) |
| `"true"` | `true` (boolean) |
| `"false"` | `false` (boolean) |
| `"null"` | `null` |
| `"My App"` | `"My App"` (string) |
| `'"3000"'` | `"3000"` (string — quotes opt out of coercion) |
| `'"a \\"b\\" c"'` | `'a "b" c'` (string — `\"` unescaped) |
| `""` | `""` (empty string passes through) |
| `undefined` | `undefined` |

`true` / `false` / `null` are case-sensitive. `True`, `YES`, `1` stay as strings.

`${VAR}` is resolved at parse time against the internal store first, then `process.env`. A reference that resolves in NEITHER place throws, naming the key:

```ts
parseValue("prefix:${NOT_DEFINED}:suffix");
// Error: Cannot resolve ${NOT_DEFINED}: "NOT_DEFINED" is not defined in the loaded
// env data or in process.env. Forward references are not supported — declare
// "NOT_DEFINED" before the line that references it, or in .env.shared, which loads first.
```

Before 1.3.0 this returned the literal string `"prefix:undefined:suffix"` — value corruption rather than a missing value, since the app starts and then fails much later (`postgres://undefined/app`).

Forward references are unsupported: lines are processed top-to-bottom within a file, so a referenced key must come from an earlier line, from `.env.shared` (loaded first), or from `process.env`.

## env(key, defaultValue?)

```ts
const env: {
  (key: string, defaultValue?: any): any;
  all(): Record<string, any>;
};
```

Lookup order: **internal store → `process.env` → `defaultValue`** (or `undefined`).

```ts
env("APP_PORT");          // 3000
env("APP_PORT", 8080);    // 3000 (loaded value wins)
env("NODE_ENV");          // "production" (from process.env — no file declares it)
env("MISSING", 0);        // 0
env.all();                // { APP_PORT: 3000, ... }  (by reference — do not mutate)
```

`env` uses `key in envData` (not `??`), so a deliberately-loaded `null` is preserved and distinguishable from a missing key: with `EST_TIME=null` in the file, `env("EST_TIME", "fallback")` returns `null`.

A value that comes from the `process.env` step is coerced the same way a file value is (`"8080"` → `8080`, `"true"` → `true`, `"null"` → `null`) so a key's type does not depend on where it came from. That coercion is narrower than `parseValue`: no quote stripping, no `${VAR}` interpolation, and values with significant leading/trailing whitespace pass through untouched.

Before 1.3.0 `env()` never consulted `process.env`, so a platform-injected variable that no `.env` file declared returned its default forever — including `env("NODE_ENV")` before `loadEnv()` had run at all.

`env.all()` returns the loaded store only. It is deliberately NOT merged with `process.env`; use `env(key)` for the fallback.

## resetEnv()

```ts
function resetEnv(): void
```

1. Clears every key from the internal store.
2. Deletes every `process.env` key that `loadEnvFile` wrote since module load (tracked internally in a `Set`).
3. Copies the initial `process.env` snapshot (captured at module import time) back onto `process.env`.

The net effect is a true "back to t0" for anything the loader added. Keys that callers set directly on `process.env`, without going through `loadEnv` / `loadEnvFile`, are not tracked and survive the reset — the caller owns their own additions.

## File-format rules

- `KEY=value` — type-coerced.
- `KEY="value"` — string, even if it looks numeric.
- `KEY="value with spaces"` — quotes preserve whitespace.
- `KEY="value \"with\" escapes"` — `\"` becomes `"`.
- `KEY=${OTHER}` — interpolation of an already-loaded key, or of a `process.env` key. Throws if neither has it.
- `# comment line` — ignored.
- Blank lines — ignored.
- `KEY=` — yields `["KEY", ""]`.
- `JUST_A_KEY` — ignored (no `=`).

## NODE_ENV semantics

```bash
# Filesystem
.env
.env.shared
.env.development
.env.production
.env.staging
```

```ts
process.env.NODE_ENV = "production";
loadEnv();
// Loads .env.shared first, then .env.production (overwrites shared keys).

process.env.NODE_ENV = "staging";
loadEnv();
// Loads .env.shared first, then .env.staging.

process.env.NODE_ENV = "test";
loadEnv();
// Loads .env.shared first; .env.test does not exist, so falls back to .env.
```

## Override semantics

```ts
loadEnv();                              // override: true (default)
process.env.APP_PORT;                   // "3000"  — string (Node coerces on assignment)
env("APP_PORT");                        // 3000    — number (typed store)
```

```ts
loadEnv(undefined, { override: false });
process.env.APP_PORT;                   // unchanged (was undefined → still undefined)
env("APP_PORT");                        // 3000
```

Override only affects `process.env`. The internal store is populated either way. It does NOT control precedence — see the `precedence` section above.

## Precedence semantics

```ts
process.env.APP_HOST = "injected-host";   // e.g. Kubernetes
// .env contains: APP_HOST=localhost

loadEnv();                                            // precedence: "file-wins" (default)
env("APP_HOST");                                      // "localhost"      — the file won
process.env.APP_HOST;                                 // "localhost"      — overwritten

loadEnv(undefined, { precedence: "process-wins" });
env("APP_HOST");                                      // "injected-host"  — the platform won
process.env.APP_HOST;                                 // "injected-host"  — left intact
```

Keys the file declares that the environment does NOT provide are loaded normally under both settings.

## Known limitations

- **`env()` returns `any`** — no type-safe key narrowing.
- **Forward references are unsupported.** `A=${B}` with `B` declared on a later line throws; declare `B` first (or in `.env.shared`, or in `process.env`).
- **Numeric coercion is `!isNaN(value)`-based**, so a zero-padded value like `0123` becomes the number `123`. Quote it (`KEY="0123"`) to keep it a string.
- **`env.all()` returns the store by reference** — mutating the returned object mutates the store.
- **The default `precedence` is `"file-wins"`**, which lets a baked-in `.env` file override platform-injected variables. Pass `"process-wins"` in containers. v2.0 flips the default.

The four defects documented in `src/__tests__/known-bugs.test.ts` (the `null` collapse, the quoted-`#`-with-comment mis-trim, the double `parseValue` call, and `resetEnv` leaving keys behind) were all fixed in 1.2.4; that file now pins the corrected behaviour. The four defects from the 2026-08-10 report are covered in `src/__tests__/process-env.test.ts`.

## Patterns

### Boot at process start

```ts
import { loadEnv } from "@mongez/dotenv";

loadEnv();  // before requiring anything else that reads env
```

### Per-environment config with shared defaults

```bash
# .env.shared
APP_NAME="My App"

# .env.development
DB_URL="mongodb://localhost/dev"
DEBUG=true

# .env.production
DB_URL="mongodb+srv://prod-host/app?retryWrites=true&w=majority"
DEBUG=false
```

```ts
loadEnv();
env("DB_URL");
```

### Read typed values

```ts
const port: number  = env("APP_PORT", 3000);
const debug: boolean = env("DEBUG", false);
const name: string = env("APP_NAME", "App");
```

### Lower-level load by absolute path

```ts
import { loadEnvFile } from "@mongez/dotenv";

loadEnvFile("/etc/myapp/secrets.env", /* override */ false);
```

### Containerised deploy

```ts
import { loadEnv, env } from "@mongez/dotenv";

loadEnv(undefined, { precedence: "process-wins" });

env("DATABASE_URL");  // the value the platform injected, not the baked-in .env line
env("APP_NAME");      // from .env — the platform does not set it
```

## What this package does NOT do

- Validation / schema. Use `zod` / `valibot` on top of `env()` if you need it.
- Type-safe key narrowing. `env("KEY")` returns `any`.
- Async / dynamic re-loading.
- Cookies / browser storage. This is a Node-only filesystem reader.
